title: Lightweight SIEM
tagline: Phishing and scam protection for the people in your family who are most likely to be targeted.
summary: A subscription service for non-technical people — often parents and grandparents. It scans their email for phishing, scores every suspicious message from 1 to 10 with a plain-language explanation, and alerts a linked family member so they can step in before money or credentials are lost.
problem: Enterprise SIEMs are built for security teams. The people who actually lose money to phishing are often retirees with no security team at all — and the relative who would help has no visibility until it is too late. This project is a deliberately small detection and alerting pipeline built around one relationship: one protected person, one or more family monitors.
approach: A rule-based heuristic engine scores each message for brand impersonation, look-alike and punycode domains, IP-literal links, URL shorteners, abused TLDs on links and senders, free-webmail senders claiming to be a bank, urgency language, gift-card payment requests and fake renewal/refund callback scams. Every score ships with a human-readable rationale and a threat category, never a bare number.

Gmail connects through OAuth 2.0 with the narrowest scope that supports the design. Access and refresh tokens are encrypted at rest, state is protected by a CSRF cookie, and only message headers, sender and links feed the first-pass scoring.

The monitor dashboard is a React and TypeScript app. Everything that came from a phishing email is treated as attacker-controlled: it renders as plain text only, and flagged links are shown inert, never clickable.
highlights: Privacy-first design: data minimization, explicit consent from the protected person, and a defined path for what the monitor can and cannot see.

Accounts with consent-based family linking: the protected person issues a single-use invite code, either side can revoke, and every endpoint enforces who may see whose alerts. Sessions use httpOnly cookies holding a token whose hash alone is stored, with login throttling and an Origin-check CSRF defence.
Detection tuned against both scams and ordinary mail: gift-card and fake-renewal scams are caught, while retail gift-card ads, real receipts and mailing lists like Google Groups are not flagged.
Protection history shows emails checked vs. threats caught per day and a breakdown by threat type, built on a scan log that stores no message content — a test pins its columns.
Gmail OAuth flow with Fernet-encrypted tokens, automatic refresh, and manual-trigger ingestion into the same scoring engine.
106 automated tests, with every external service mocked — 42 of them attack the sign-in, session and family-access rules directly.

Public demo deployed to GitHub Pages by GitHub Actions: no backend, a strict Content Security Policy, and sample data generated from the real detection engine, with a test that fails if the two drift apart.
next: Verify the Gmail connection against a live inbox and add background polling.
Alert delivery by email, push and SMS, plus password reset over email.
Browser extension for link checks at click time.
Threat-intelligence lookups and AI-written risk narratives, sent only after a heuristic flag.
